# Operator Law Intake — Shadow-Cat Temporal Exchant and Cross-Level Callings

**Date:** 2026-07-28
**Status:** `PROVISIONAL_UNNUMBERED | OPERATOR_CANON | LAW_70_EXTENSION | LIRIS_CROSSWALK_COMPLETE`

## Exact operator statements

> massIve update shadowcats have levels of temporal exchant

> THEY call other levels of shadow cats like the callings

Capitalization, spelling, and the word `exchant` are preserved exactly. This intake does not
silently replace `exchant` with `exchange`, `enchantment`, or another English word.

## The correction

Law 70 establishes that shadow cats have **levels**. The later operator statement adds the
missing relation: the levels are not isolated bins. **A shadow-cat level can call another
shadow-cat level in the manner of the existing callings.**

That makes the level system a graph during play rather than a scalar ladder. Existing
chain canon defines a calling as an unordered join, and the new words do not yet bind a
direction:

```text
shadow-cat level A --calling join-- shadow-cat level B
                   --calling join-- shadow-cat level C

both endpoints remain separately addressed; direction is unresolved
```

A calling does not, by its name alone, promote A into B, overwrite either endpoint, delete
the source, or imply a one-way chronological jump. The exact executable meaning of
`temporal exchant` remains owned by the operator/fabric contract.

## Existing structural antecedents

This relation was not invented from the new name. The existing Combined Book already
preserves all of the following:

- **Callings chain into callings; chains of chains close into balls.**
- **The callings are calling each other** and wrap together like a buckyball.
- **The shadow cat is the positive that feeds the calling chain**, feeds the rime spheres,
  and creates calling chains that call other calling chains.
- Each shadow cat has a **gradient colour that represents its level in shadow-cat time,
  space, and colour**.
- Frozen and playable states are each addressable at past, present, and future spherical
  orientations; watcher and reader can operate in either state.

The new operator statement closes those antecedents into one recursive relation: the same
calling behavior already recorded between calling chains also exists **between shadow-cat
levels**.

## Axes that must remain separate

The following are not aliases and must not be collapsed into one `level` integer:

| Axis | Meaning retained |
|---|---|
| shadow-cat identity | the addressed cat/body/function |
| shadow-cat level | one level in its level family |
| calling edge | the join between retained endpoints; direction unresolved |
| temporal exchant | the exact operator-named relation; semantics not silently expanded |
| temporal orientation | past, present, or future, spherically |
| runtime state | frozen or playable |
| colour | continuous RGB/rainbow gradient |
| translucency | continuous tie/shell/white-space relation |
| space and energy | routed coordinates, not inferred from the level number |
| rime direction | the active spherical/wave relation |
| PID and receipt | identity, lineage, source seat, and proof stratum |

## Separation from the Law 70 scalar model

Law 70's `(n-1)/n` table is a claimed spectrum of one lighthouse software operator grouped
by distinct vector widths. Even if that bounded operator calculation is confirmed, it is
only a **count projection** of `n` populated levels. It does not define the identity,
gradient, temporal orientation, frozen/playable state, or cross-level calling semantics of
the operator's shadow cats.

The Liris audit resolves that software scope more exactly. For `n` equally populated,
strictly nested levels, `(n-1)/n` is the transient eigenvalue of the **widest-exclusive
coordinate shell**. It is not the full spectrum and not a global survival fraction. The
published operator also contains fixed modes with eigenvalue `1` and a common-core mode
with eigenvalue `0`. Law 70 is therefore the synchronous **NO-CALL baseline**. Once levels
call other levels, the dynamic spectrum depends on the call graph, coupling, phase/order,
delay, recursion/cycle structure, and carried component—not `n` alone.

Therefore:

```text
level count is not level identity
operator eigenvalue is not a calling
contraction is not temporal exchant
```

## Minimal publication contract

Until an owning executable contract arrives, every recorded temporal-exchant calling must
preserve at least:

```text
endpoint_a_shadowcat_pid
endpoint_a_level
endpoint_b_shadowcat_pid
endpoint_b_level
calling_id
direction_if_bound
endpoint_a_time_orientation
endpoint_b_time_orientation
endpoint_a_state
endpoint_b_state
colour_gradient_address
translucency_gradient_address
space_energy_rime_address
seat_and_vantage
source_slice_sha256
receipt_sha256
```

Unknown values remain held. No field may be synthesized from another merely because their
counts match.

A future matched control must keep level identities, populations, and marginals fixed while
breaking only temporal endpoint pairing and any order later bound by the executable
contract. That tests the calling relation without replacing the level universe.
